inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: Organizers say an estimated 8 million people took part in more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, protesting President Donald Trump’s leadership. That kind of nationwide mobilization shows how deeply people are concerned about power being concentrated at the top—and how many see defending democracy as inseparable from protecting the people most exposed to political harm. Organizers say turnout exceeded the previous demonstrations in October by about one million participants and 600 events. There’s no official count from US authorities, but the scale of the organizing itself is a powerful signal.
